the presence of microbial colonization at birth in the airways of ventilated infants is associated with an increased inflammatory response in the trachea and bronchi, which may be of clinical relevance.
the inflammatory response in the airways of colonized infants is more pronounced than in the airways from non-colonized infants.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inflammatory response in preterm infants is associated with microbial colonization at birth.

the presence of Ureaplasma spp. in the airways of preterm infants at birth is associated to an increased inflammatory response of the lung, which is reflected by increased concentrations of IL-1, IL-8, leukotriens and elastase in the trachea.
the airway colonisation at birth with U. urealyticum and/or bacteria is associated with an increased risk for developing BPD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the airway colonisation of U urealyticicum or bacteria at birth was associated with an inflammatory response.
the presence of Ureaplasma in the respiratory tract of newborns is not necessarily associated with clinical disease.
we have identified a new biomarker that may help identify infants at high risk for developing bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD).
